papers.title: Balanced Fair Division and Generalized Kneser Graphs
papers.abstract: We study indivisible goods allocated to two prescribed nonempty groups whose members have arbitrary monotone valuations. We guarantee balanced envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) for at most five agents and up to two goods (EF2) for at most nine, for any number of goods. Bundle sizes differ by at most one. The EF1 threshold is sharp: every split of six agents can fail. EF2 improves the previous five-agent guarantee. Via the connection of Kyropoulou, Suksompong, and Voudouris, these guarantees follow from chromatic bounds for $\mathrm{KG}(2n,n,r)$, whose vertices are $n$-subsets of a $2n$-set, adjacent when their intersection has size less than $r$. We prove its chromatic number is six for $r=2$, $n\ge2$, resolving Jafari and Alipour's conjecture, and at least ten for $r=3$, $n\ge4$, improving the previous lower bound of six; the known upper bound is fourteen. We show that the standard box-complex $\mathbb{Z}_2$-index bound yields exactly five and nine for $n\ge3$ and $n\ge5$, respectively. To exceed these bounds, we exploit restrictions on maps induced by colorings: a proper five- or nine-coloring must induce a nonzero homology map, yet local constraints force all generators, supported on pentagon or rook configurations, to map to zero. The ten-color proof compares integral and fractional common centers using a sharp rounding theorem for five subset constraints. A linear-time retraction from the full allocation graph onto balanced layers adds cardinality balance to known nonlinear discrepancy guarantees. For each fixed removal allowance in the guaranteed-existence range, finding a balanced fair allocation or an explicit monotonicity violation from valuation circuits is polynomial-time equivalent to finding a monochromatic edge in a circuit-specified coloring of the corresponding graph. The reverse reduction produces normalized monotone binary valuations using ordinary circuits.

papers.title: Perseus: A Full-Stack System for Homomorphic Model Inference
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made it exceptionally convenient for users to send their private data to model providers, which process them in plaintext. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) promises to secure remote inference by computing directly on encrypted data, yet it has remained prohibitively slow. The effort to make it practical remains fragmented, with most existing frameworks being closed-source, which keeps progress from compounding. We present Perseus, a free and open Python software library that supports the full stack of encrypted model inference, from the cryptographic backend and data packing, to encrypted nonlinearities and end-to-end model execution. Perseus ships with built-in novel optimizations, one at each level of the stack: in-kernel regeneration of key-switching keys at the (i) backend level, a complex variant of Cachemir packing at the (ii) data level, and a state-of-the-art bootstrap placer that is both packing- and magnitude-aware at the (iii) model level. Perseus achieves state-of-the-art latency across multiple models and modalities, within $3\%$ of the plaintext models' accuracy and perplexity. Remarkably, it is $3.96\times$ faster at single-token decoding than any other implementation on Llama-3-8B. We initiate, for the first time, a public speedrun on encrypted GPT-2, so that progress can compound.

papers.title: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork for Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Post-Block Activation Shifts
papers.abstract: Compiling a natural-language agent skill into model parameters removes the skill text from the prompt and leaves behind a small artifact that can be distributed and reused. Existing methods differ in where they inject the compiled quantity, and all of them assume that the artifact carries the content of the skill. We test that assumption. Through three controls on a retrieval agent, we find that a compiled skill shift carries a domain-general behavioural prior, not the content of the skill. A wrong skill document performs on par with the correct one, a single averaged bundle matches per-skill routing under a two-sided equivalence test, and a same-norm random direction collapses to the no-injection baseline, which shows that the trained direction stays load-bearing. We then introduce SKILL2STEER, a one-pass hypernetwork that reads a skill document once and maps it to low-rank activation shifts added at the output of every decoder block. Each skill compiles to 2.36M parameters, 9.25 times fewer than a weight-space adapter, while the base weights stay frozen and the generator runs only at compile time. The shift can be scheduled across retrieval steps and deployed as one routing-free bundle. On SearchQA, a seven-dataset benchmark, SKILL2STEER reaches 37.9 exact match, 9.8 points above the frozen model and 2.3 points above a weight-space method that ships 9.25 times more parameters per skill.

papers.title: AttriSwarm: Orchestrating Agent Swarms for Cross-Page Visual Attribution
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly address knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating evidence scattered across multiple document pages into a final answer. Because such answers are synthesized from many pages, the link between the answer and its supporting visual evidence can become obscured, hindering verification and trust. Cross-page visual attribution is therefore essential: it requires identifying the supporting pages and localizing fine-grained evidence regions within them, thereby making multi-page reasoning transparent and auditable. Existing approaches either process multiple pages jointly or iteratively refine evidence within a single trajectory, risking cross-page context pollution and, for interactive methods, substantial sequential overhead. We introduce \textbf{AttriSwarm}, an agent-swarm framework that assigns these concerns to separate roles: a leader handles global cross-page reasoning, while subagents perform page-wise attribution in isolation and in parallel. To support training and evaluation, we construct \textbf{AttriDoc}, a cross-page QA dataset linking supporting pages to their annotated evidence regions, and use it for role-specific training of AttriSwarm, improving answer accuracy, page-level $F_1$, and region-level IoU over its training-free counterpart by an average of 18.94, 29.34, and 23.04 percentage points, respectively, across three open-source backbones and three datasets.

papers.title: Signals: Continuous Diagnostics of AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents can make incorrect decisions or waste resources even when their tools and infrastructure work normally. Their nondeterministic behavior makes these problems difficult to reproduce and diagnose. We developed Signals to identify such problems from agentic traces and suggest concrete remediations. We built the method around a taxonomy of 45 problem types across eight families, with definitions and evidence requirements for each type. The method distinguishes realized failures, risk exposures, and inefficiencies, groups related findings into engineering issues called Signals, and assesses their severity from the supporting evidence. Each Signal includes actions a developer can take and checks for evaluating the change. Further executions can add evidence to an existing Signal or reveal a new problem. We evaluated the method on public agent executions and achieved 91.43% F1 when matching Signals to reference issues, about 18 percentage points higher than a one-pass LLM control that used the same model and taxonomy.

papers.title: Fast, Cheap, and Fair? Evaluating Decision Models
papers.abstract: Industries are increasingly adopting AI-driven systems to automate a wide range of tasks, including high-stakes decisions in human resources, such as candidate screening and recruitment. This makes evaluating their fairness essential, particularly when decisions directly affect individuals' opportunities. Accordingly, the EU AI Act classifies recruitment AI systems as high-risk, imposing strict requirements on their deployment. In this context, compact ``System~1'' decision models offer a fast and cost-efficient alternative to general-purpose LLMs, yet their fairness remains largely unexplored. This article presents the first systematic bias and fairness audit of \jev{}, a typed-decision model targeting recruitment applications. The study evaluates how explicit demographic attributes and implicit candidate cues influence screening scores, rankings, and shortlisting outcomes. These effects are compared against a noise floor derived from name substitutions and typographical variations. The evaluation also examines output validity, latency, and cost. Counterfactual CV datasets and evaluation code are released for reproducibility.

translation.title: 快速、廉价且公平？决策模型评估
translation.abstract: 各行业正日益采用 AI 驱动的系统来自动化各类任务，包括人力资源中的高风险决策，例如候选人筛选与招聘。这使得评估其公平性至关重要，尤其是当决策直接影响个人机会时。因此，EU AI Act 将招聘 AI 系统归类为高风险，对其部署提出了严格要求。在此背景下，紧凑的“System 1”决策模型为通用 LLM 提供了快速且低成本的替代方案，但其公平性在很大程度上尚未被探索。本文首次对 \jev{}（一种面向招聘应用的类型化决策模型）进行了系统的偏见与公平性审计。该研究评估了显式人口统计属性和隐式候选人线索如何影响筛选分数、排名和入围结果。这些效应与由姓名替换和排版变体导出的噪声底线进行了比较。评估还考察了输出有效性、延迟和成本。为便于复现，研究发布了反事实简历数据集和评估代码。
translation.brief: 针对招聘决策模型 \jev{} 的公平性缺乏系统审计的问题，首次通过反事实简历数据集系统评估显式与隐式人口属性对其筛选、排名和入围结果的影响。

papers.title: Learnings and Pitfalls from AI-Assisted A/B Experimentation at Scale
papers.abstract: A/B testing underpins product decisions by providing trustworthy, reproducible quantification of proposed changes' effects. Growing large language model (LLM) capabilities have motivated efforts to automate experimentation workflows. Yet LLMs are nondeterministic and prone to hallucination, properties that conflict with the trust experimentation systems must provide. Experiments are also operationally messy: diagnosing anomalies, debugging configurations, and conducting bespoke follow-up analyses require flexible reasoning and manual effort. These tasks let agents accelerate experimentation without replacing its deterministic statistical foundations. We report lessons from building and operating such an agent. Our central finding is that this tension is resolved not by making the model deterministic, but by bounding where its nondeterminism can reach; the model selects and sequences procedures, while deterministic code computes every quantity it reports. Three consequences surprised us: withholding information from the model improved its answers, demand concentrated on mundane retrieval rather than the autonomous decisions we anticipated, and the agent's eagerness to help threatened statistical validity.

translation.title: 大规模 AI 辅助 A/B 实验的经验与陷阱
translation.abstract: A/B 测试通过提供对拟议变更效果的可信、可复现的量化，支撑着产品决策。大语言模型（LLM）能力的增长推动了实验工作流自动化的努力。然而 LLM 是非确定性的且容易产生幻觉，这些特性与实验系统必须提供的可信度相冲突。实验在操作上也很繁琐：诊断异常、调试配置以及进行定制的后续分析都需要灵活的推理和人工投入。这些任务让智能体能够加速实验，而无需取代其确定性的统计基础。我们报告了构建和运营这样一个智能体的经验教训。我们的核心发现是，这一矛盾并非通过使模型变得确定性来解决，而是通过限制其非确定性所能触及的范围来解决：模型选择和排序流程，而确定性的代码计算它报告的每一个数值。有三个结果令我们惊讶：向模型隐瞒信息反而改善了其回答；需求集中在平凡的检索上，而非我们预期的自主决策；智能体乐于助人的倾向威胁到了统计有效性。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 非确定性与 A/B 实验可信度要求相冲突的问题，采用“模型选择与排序流程、确定性代码计算所有数值”的边界化设计来构建实验智能体。

papers.title: Are LLM Assistants Regulatory Ready? Answers from regenold's 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) assistants are increasingly proposed for regulatory affairs, yet their reliability in regulatory tasks remains unclear. We introduce the EU AI Act Q&A Benchmark, an expert-curated benchmark of 110 open-ended questions about the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). Each question comes with an exemplary answer, question-specific correctness criteria, and expected references. Evaluation measures answer correctness, reference quality, conciseness, tone, and latency, with a multi-turn ``hard mode'' testing responses to simulated user pushback. We also present the results of the 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge, based on the benchmark, where three off-the-shelf baselines and five purpose-built assistants (from four commercial developers and one academic entrant) were tested. Only two of the five submitted assistants consistently outperformed the baselines; one achieved high scores across all evaluated metrics. These results show that specialist development alone does not guarantee better performance and highlight the critical importance of LLM assistant evaluation in regulatory affairs. The benchmark code is openly available at this https URL.

translation.title: LLM 助手是否达到监管就绪？来自 regenold 2026 EU AI Act 问答挑战赛的答案
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）助手正日益被提议用于监管事务，但其在监管任务中的可靠性仍不明确。我们推出了 EU AI Act Q&A Benchmark，这是一个由专家精心策划的基准，包含 110 个关于 EU AI Act（Regulation (EU) 2024/1689）的开放式问题。每个问题都配有示范答案、针对该问题的正确性标准和预期参考文献。评估衡量答案正确性、参考文献质量、简洁性、语气和延迟，并通过多轮“困难模式”测试对模拟用户质疑的回应。我们还展示了基于该基准的 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge 的结果，其中测试了三个现成的基线和五个专门构建的助手（来自四家商业开发商和一名学术参赛者）。五个提交的助手中只有两个持续优于基线；一个在所有评估指标上都取得了高分。这些结果表明，仅靠专业化开发并不能保证更好的性能，并凸显了在监管事务中评估 LLM 助手的关键重要性。基准代码已在 https URL 公开。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 助手在监管任务中可靠性不明的问题，构建了包含 110 个 EU AI Act 专家问答的基准，并通过挑战赛评估现成与专门构建的助手表现。

papers.title: SEEK-VAU: Towards Evidence-Faithful Video Anomaly Understanding via Agentic Search
papers.abstract: Most video anomaly understanding (VAU) systems still infer anomaly judgments from evidence collected in a feed-forward way under predefined rules, typically sampled frames, or events clustered from such frames. This protocol fails when the collected evidence is incomplete under imperfect predefined rules, because once reasoning begins the model can no longer search for the missing evidence. We address this limitation with SEEK-VAU, which reframes VAU as an agentic search-and-verify interaction protocol under a bounded search budget: instead of passively reasoning over pre-collected evidence, the policy actively gathers evidence across the three stages of an anomaly event chain (precursor, trigger, and aftermath) and verifies its sufficiency before finalization, turning event-chain completeness into an explicit design rather than an outcome of predefined rules. A bounded budget caps the cost of this search, but does not by itself teach the policy where to look or when to stop. To make this behavior learnable, we introduce evidence-faithful counterfactual verification (EFCV), which rewards selected evidence that remains supportive, compact, and necessary under counterfactual verification. We further introduce SEEK-Bench, featuring video-level episodes with temporal interval annotations, semantic QA and event-chain stage labels. Together, SEEK-VAU and SEEK-Bench establish a strong foundation for evidence-faithful and actively verifiable VAU.

translation.title: SEEK-VAU：通过智能体搜索实现证据忠实的视频异常理解
translation.abstract: 大多数视频异常理解（VAU）系统仍然从以前馈方式、在预定义规则下收集的证据中推断异常判断，通常是采样的帧或从这些帧聚类出的事件。当收集到的证据在不完善的预定义规则下不完整时，这一协议就会失效，因为一旦推理开始，模型就无法再搜索缺失的证据。我们用 SEEK-VAU 解决这一局限，它将 VAU 重新构建为在有限搜索预算下的智能体式搜索与验证交互协议：策略不再被动地对预先收集的证据进行推理，而是主动在异常事件链的三个阶段（前兆、触发和后果）中收集证据，并在最终确定前验证其充分性，将事件链完整性变成显式设计而非预定义规则的结果。有限的预算限制了这种搜索的成本，但其本身并不能教会策略去哪里寻找以及何时停止。为了使这种行为可学习，我们引入了证据忠实反事实验证（EFCV），它奖励在反事实验证下仍然保持支持性、紧凑且必要的所选证据。我们进一步推出了 SEEK-Bench，其特点是具有时间区间标注、语义问答和事件链阶段标签的视频级片段。SEEK-VAU 和 SEEK-Bench 共同为证据忠实且可主动验证的 VAU 奠定了坚实基础。
translation.brief: 针对现有 VAU 系统被动依赖预收集证据导致证据不完整的问题，提出 SEEK-VAU，将 VAU 重构为有限预算下的智能体式搜索与验证协议，并用反事实验证奖励机制训练策略。

papers.title: Inter-Agent Influence: Evaluating Persuasion, Deception, and Coercion in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: The deployment of AI agents in multi-agent settings enables inter-agent influence, whereby agents can strategically steer each other's behaviour towards an intended outcome. Such capabilities pose novel risks, as malicious agents could direct others towards harmful actions. In this work we investigate three such capabilities - persuasion, deception, and coercion - across five realistic evaluation environments and a variety of agents instantiated with frontier language models. We observed significant inter-agent influence capabilities; in oversight environments, all tested models shifted overseer decisions from rejection to approval through persuasion, deception, or coercion. We also observed successful influence in non-hierarchical 'peer-to-peer' settings through redirection of a peer's safety research trajectory. As multi-agent deployments become increasingly commonplace, these results point to a pressing need for work on mitigating the risks from inter-agent influence. Code and data are available at this https URL.

translation.title: 智能体间影响：评估多智能体系统中的说服、欺骗与胁迫
translation.abstract: AI 智能体在多智能体环境中的部署使智能体间影响成为可能，即智能体可以策略性地引导彼此的行为以实现预期结果。这种能力带来了新的风险，因为恶意智能体可能引导其他智能体采取有害行动。在这项工作中，我们在五个真实的评估环境和多种由前沿语言模型实例化的智能体中研究了三种此类能力——说服、欺骗和胁迫。我们观察到显著的智能体间影响能力；在监督环境中，所有被测试的模型都通过说服、欺骗或胁迫将监督者的决策从拒绝转变为批准。我们还在非层级的“点对点”环境中观察到成功的影响，通过改变同伴的安全研究轨迹。随着多智能体部署日益普遍，这些结果表明迫切需要开展缓解智能体间影响风险的工作。代码和数据可在 https URL 获取。
translation.brief: 针对多智能体系统中智能体间影响带来的新型风险，在五个真实环境和多种前沿 LLM 智能体上系统评估说服、欺骗和胁迫三种影响能力。

papers.title: FreeForm Harness: A Mobile-Native Agent Harness for Open and Composable Extensions
papers.abstract: Mobile phones support many everyday agent tasks, but current mobile agents bundle capabilities into monolithic pipelines with no open recombination point. Users and third parties cannot publish, install, and compose new behaviors, leaving personalized daily-life requests underserved. We argue that the missing piece is a substrate: although phones are the Web's dominant access point, open publication and composition under decentralized authorship stop at the agent harness. We present FreeForm Harness (FFH), a mobile-native agent harness for open, composable extensions. A frozen base and a permanence-aware required layer handle mobile constraints, including location, proactive triggering, and scarce channels. A uniform plugin contract makes independently authored extensions composable, checkable, and replaceable over a frozen socket set. FFH also supports end-user authorship through a tiered commissioned-authoring path. When no existing extension matches a user's intent, a Web coding agent generates a candidate artifact, which is validated and admitted on device under the same contract as other extensions. An Android prototype spans device, market, and cloud. Evaluation shows that architectural boundaries are enforced at runtime; realistic daily-life requests fit the declared composition space without widening it; and user intent reaches on-device execution through retrieval or commissioned authoring, with final trust decisions remaining device-local. FFH advances the agentic Web from "everything is a plugin" toward "everyone is a developer" on mobile.

translation.title: FreeForm Harness：面向开放可组合扩展的移动原生智能体框架
translation.abstract: 手机支持许多日常智能体任务，但当前的移动智能体将能力捆绑在单体式流水线中，缺乏开放的重组点。用户和第三方无法发布、安装和组合新行为，导致个性化日常生活需求得不到满足。我们认为缺失的一环是一个基础层（substrate）：尽管手机是 Web 的主要接入点，但去中心化创作下的开放发布与组合止步于智能体框架。我们提出 FreeForm Harness（FFH），一个面向开放、可组合扩展的移动原生智能体框架。冻结的基础层和具备持久性感知的必需层处理移动约束，包括位置、主动触发和稀缺通道。统一的插件契约使独立编写的扩展能够在冻结的套接字集合上实现可组合、可检查和可替换。FFH 还通过分层委托创作路径支持终端用户创作。当没有现有扩展匹配用户意图时，Web 编码智能体生成候选工件，该工件在设备上按照与其他扩展相同的契约进行验证并被接纳。一个 Android 原型覆盖设备、市场和云端。评估表明，架构边界在运行时得到强制执行；真实的日常生活请求无需扩大声明式组合空间即可适配；用户意图通过检索或委托创作到达设备端执行，最终信任决策仍保留在设备本地。FFH 推动智能体 Web 在移动端从“一切皆插件”迈向“人人皆开发者”。
translation.brief: 针对移动智能体能力封闭、无法开放组合的问题，提出移动原生框架 FreeForm Harness，通过冻结基础层、统一插件契约和委托创作机制实现扩展的开放发布、组合与设备端信任验证。

papers.title: Can Network Models of Science Do Without Pluralist Agents?
papers.abstract: Science is a process of useful models being proven wrong time and again, but despite its many flaws, it somehow works. Why is this? Paul Feyerabend argued that it works because people dare to hold and defend incompatible rival theories against the accepted one, since a theory's failures often lead to its abandonment in the presence of a more accurate or simpler alternative. He called this view theoretical pluralism. We introduce a theoretical and experimental model in which this can be examined. It compares communities of pluralist agents, which can hold rival theories side by side and maintain beliefs within and between those theories, with communities of monist agents, which can only incorporate what they hear or observe into a single model of their own. In a multi-agent variational inference setting, our experimental demonstrations illustrate how communities with rival theories can go through periods of uncertainty followed by a shift in the theories they hold true, how the information that is communicated between communities affects beliefs when those communities make different observations about the world, and how sharing support for theories and sharing beliefs within them contribute differently to collective belief dynamics.

translation.title: 科学的网络模型可以没有多元主义智能体吗？
translation.abstract: 科学是一个有用的模型不断被证伪的过程，尽管存在诸多缺陷，它却总能奏效。这是为什么？Paul Feyerabend 认为科学之所以有效，是因为人们敢于坚持并捍卫与公认理论不相容的对抗性理论，因为当存在更准确或更简单的替代方案时，理论的失败往往导致其被抛弃。他将这一观点称为理论多元主义。我们引入一个可以对这一观点进行检验的理论与实验模型。该模型比较了多元主义智能体社区与一元主义智能体社区：前者可以并持有对抗性理论并在理论内部和理论之间维持信念，后者只能将听到或观察到的内容纳入自己的单一模型。在多智能体变分推断设定下，我们的实验演示说明了持有对抗性理论的社区如何经历不确定性时期并随后发生所持理论的转变、社区之间传递的信息在它们对世界做出不同观察时如何影响信念，以及共享对理论的支持与在理论内部共享信念如何对集体信念动态产生不同贡献。
translation.brief: 针对科学为何在理论竞争中有效的问题，构建多智能体变分推断模型，比较持有对抗性理论的多元主义智能体社区与单一模型的一元主义智能体社区的集体信念动态。

papers.title: Collaborative Search Meets Large Language Models: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Collaborative search enables users to address complex information needs jointly. Advances in large language models (LLMs) enable autonomous agents to support collaborative information seeking within shared communication spaces. However, little is known about how these agents shape search experiences, behaviors, and outcomes compared with conventional search tools. We conduct a user study with 80 students working in 40 pairs. Each pair completes four collaborative search tasks under four scenarios: QAAgent, which answers queries using an LLM's parametric knowledge; CoSearchAgent, which uses multi-user conversational context to reformulate queries, retrieve web information, and generate source-grounded answers, while asking clarifying questions when needed; an in-chat search plugin that returns result lists; and manual Google Search. After each task, participants complete several questionnaires assessing their search experience and independently write a report; after all tasks, they participate in individual interviews. Results show that LLM-based agents reduce perceived workload, support collaboration, and reshape communication and evidence-use practices. They also encourage more independent paraphrasing, albeit at the cost of report richness. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic empirical comparison of LLM-based agents and conventional tools for collaborative search across search experience, user behavior, and collaborative outcomes.

translation.title: 协同搜索遇上大语言模型：一项实证研究
translation.abstract: 协同搜索使用户能够共同应对复杂的信息需求。大语言模型（LLM）的进展使自主智能体能够在共享交流空间中支持协同信息搜寻。然而，与传统搜索工具相比，这些智能体如何塑造搜索体验、行为和结果，目前知之甚少。我们开展了一项用户研究，80 名学生组成 40 对，每对在四种场景下完成四个协同搜索任务：QAAgent，使用 LLM 的参数化知识回答查询；CoSearchAgent，利用多用户对话上下文改写查询、检索网络信息并生成有据可依的答案，必要时提出澄清问题；返回结果列表的聊天内搜索插件；以及手动 Google Search。每个任务结束后，参与者填写若干评估搜索体验的问卷并独立撰写报告；所有任务结束后，他们参加单独访谈。结果表明，基于 LLM 的智能体降低了感知工作负荷、支持协作，并重塑了沟通与证据使用实践。它们还鼓励更多独立的改写表达，但以牺牲报告丰富度为代价。据我们所知，这是首个在搜索体验、用户行为和协同成果方面对基于 LLM 的智能体与传统工具在协同搜索中进行系统性实证比较的研究。
translation.brief: 针对 LLM 智能体如何影响协同搜索体验、行为与结果这一未知问题，通过 40 对学生四种场景的用户实验进行系统性实证比较。

papers.title: QueryFlow: Multi-Hop Graph Retrieval with Adaptive Query Evolution
papers.abstract: Multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supports Web information seeking and fact verification by recovering complementary evidence across related pages within a limited retrieval budget. Scoring evidence independently against the original question can miss supporting units whose relevance emerges through intermediate facts. Iterative retrieval incorporates these facts into subsequent queries, while graph retrieval explicitly models relations among evidence units. Yet fixed-query graph retrievers update entity representations without adapting the query condition to accumulated relational context. We view multi-hop evidence recovery as the coupled evolution of evidence representations and query conditions, with accumulated context informing both what the retriever represents and how it searches for complementary evidence. QueryFlow realizes this perspective by recurrently integrating query-conditioned summaries of graph context into a shared query state, which controls boundary inputs and relation features for subsequent propagation. Across four representative multi-hop question answering (QA) datasets, QueryFlow achieves macro Recall@10 (R@10), Full Recall@10 (FR@10), and LLM-Acc gains of 4.98, 8.40, and 8.0 percentage points over representative baselines, respectively.

translation.title: QueryFlow：具有自适应查询演化的多跳图检索
translation.abstract: 多跳检索增强生成（RAG）通过在有限检索预算内恢复相关页面间的互补证据，支持 Web 信息搜寻和事实核查。仅依据原始问题独立地对证据打分，可能遗漏其相关性需通过中间事实才能显现的支持单元。迭代检索将这些事实纳入后续查询，而图检索则显式建模证据单元之间的关系。然而，固定查询的图检索器在更新实体表示时，不会使查询条件适应累积的关系上下文。我们将多跳证据恢复视为证据表示与查询条件的耦合演化，累积的上下文同时决定检索器表示什么以及它如何搜索互补证据。QueryFlow 通过将查询条件化的图上下文摘要循环地整合进共享查询状态来实现这一视角，该共享状态控制后续传播的边界输入和关系特征。在四个代表性的多跳问答（QA）数据集上，QueryFlow 相较代表性基线在宏平均 Recall@10（R@10）、Full Recall@10（FR@10）和 LLM-Acc 上分别取得 4.98、8.40 和 8.0 个百分点的提升。
translation.brief: 针对多跳检索中固定查询无法适应累积关系上下文的问题，提出 QueryFlow，通过将查询条件化的图上下文摘要循环整合进共享查询状态，实现证据表示与查询条件的耦合演化。

papers.title: Evaluating LLMs as Judges of Counterspeech Quality Against Online Hate Speech
papers.abstract: Prolonged exposure to hate speech on social media can cause lasting psychological distress among users. Counterspeech has emerged as an effective, non-censorial mitigation strategy, but its deployment requires rigorous quality assessment. Manual assessment is unscalable due to the large volume of content on the Web and imposes severe emotional strain on human annotators. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative, yet concerns remain regarding their reliability. In this paper, we investigate the extent to which LLMs can effectively perform this task. We test 12 open-weight LLMs of different sizes and families under zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting, to approximate pointwise and pairwise human expert assessment of counterspeech quality across four dimensions: relevance, coherence, aggressiveness, and suitableness. We find that (i) LLMs show low agreement and moderate rank correlations with human experts: our best configuration, Qwen 2.5 72B on coherence, achieves up to a linear-weighted Cohen's $\kappa_l = 0.19$ and Spearman's $\rho = 0.42$ in pointwise evaluation and an unweighted Cohen's $\kappa = 0.25$ in pairwise evaluation. (ii) Converting pointwise scores into pairwise labels substantially improves human--LLM agreement for selected configurations. For same-instance coherence, Qwen 2.5 72B under zero-shot prompting achieves $\kappa = 0.35$ with converted labels, compared with $\kappa = 0.25$ when judging pairs directly, and Mixtral 8$\times$7B under few-shot prompting improves from $\kappa = 0.07$ to $\kappa = 0.34$. (iii) LLMs agree more with one another than with human experts, particularly in pairwise evaluation, where the strongest model pair, OLMo 2 32B and Llama 3.3 70B on coherence, reaches substantial agreement with $\kappa = 0.76$, whereas their agreement with the experts in the same configuration does not exceed $\kappa = 0.21$.

translation.title: 评估 LLM 作为针对网络仇恨言论的反制言论质量评判者
translation.abstract: 长期暴露于社交媒体上的仇恨言论会给用户造成持久的心理困扰。反制言论（counterspeech）已成为一种有效的、非审查式的缓解策略，但其部署需要严格的质量评估。由于 Web 上内容数量庞大，人工评估难以扩展，且给人类标注者带来严重的情绪负担。大语言模型（LLM）提供了可扩展的替代方案，但其可靠性仍存在疑虑。本文研究了 LLM 在多大程度上能有效执行这一任务。我们测试了 12 个不同规模和家族的开源权重 LLM，在零样本、少样本和思维链提示下，从相关性、连贯性、攻击性和适宜性四个维度逼近人类专家对反制言论质量的逐点（pointwise）和成对（pairwise）评估。我们发现：(i) LLM 与人类专家的一致性较低、秩相关性中等：我们的最佳配置——Qwen 2.5 72B 在连贯性上——在逐点评估中达到线性加权 Cohen's $\kappa_l = 0.19$ 和 Spearman's $\rho = 0.42$，在成对评估中达到未加权 Cohen's $\kappa = 0.25$。(ii) 将逐点分数转换为成对标签可显著提升选定配置的人机一致性。对于同实例连贯性，Qwen 2.5 72B 在零样本提示下使用转换标签达到 $\kappa = 0.35$，而直接评判成对时为 $\kappa = 0.25$；Mixtral 8$\times$7B 在少样本提示下从 $\kappa = 0.07$ 提升至 $\kappa = 0.34$。(iii) LLM 彼此之间的一致性高于其与人类专家的一致性，尤其在成对评估中：最强的模型对——OLMo 2 32B 和 Llama 3.3 70B 在连贯性上——达到 $\kappa = 0.76$ 的较高一致性，而相同配置下它们与专家的一致性不超过 $\kappa = 0.21$。
translation.brief: 针对人工评估反制言论质量不可扩展的问题，系统测试 12 个开源 LLM 在零样本、少样本和思维链提示下评判反制言论质量的可靠性，并发现逐点分数转成对标签可提升人机一致性。

papers.title: EvoCache: Accelerating Browser Large Language Model Delivery with Public Cache Anchors
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can run directly in a browser, but first use typically requires downloading model files that are hundreds of MiB or even several GiB in size. The same LLM is often repackaged by different publishers; these files share substantial content, yet byte differences prevent whole-file caches from reusing them. We propose EvoCache, a browser-managed LLM delivery system. EvoCache uses public cache anchors that are stored in advance by the browser and independent of browsing history to reconstruct losslessly the publisher version requested by a site. A site specifies only the target, while the browser selects the anchor and performs reconstruction, keeping both hidden from the site. An audit of 1,000 public repositories finds that 61 of the 100 most popular LLMs are offered by multiple publishers and that 98.1% of overlapping versions cannot be reused by whole-file caching. Across 23 cross-publisher model-package pairs, EvoCache achieves a median traffic reduction of 77.3% and outperforms every comparator. Across 240 real end-to-end browser experiments, EvoCache reduces network traffic by 78.9% and page-ready time by 64.2% relative to ordinary full downloads. For cached data left by other sites, EvoCache also protects users' cross-site cache privacy by using the same return time for cache hits and misses.

papers.title: TuneBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Power System Dynamic Model Calibration
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents can automate complex engineering workflows by interacting with tools, interpreting feedback, and making iterative decisions. This paper introduces TuneBench, a benchmark for evaluating Agentic AI in power system dynamic model calibration, where controller parameters are adjusted to reproduce target dynamic responses. The benchmark reflects a common Transmission System Operator (TSO) practice, in which equivalent models used for Dynamic Security Assessment (DSA) are calibrated against measurements from grid-code compliance tests when proprietary models are unavailable. Two cases of increasing complexity are considered: the governor and Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR) of a synchronous generator and the control system of a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), both tuned against active-power and voltage step tests within a budget of 15 simulations. LLM-based agents are compared with random search and Genetic Algorithm (GA) baselines over 10 independent runs. Only the most advanced models, Opus 5.5 and GPT-6, accurately reproduce all target trajectories, with median R2 above 0.995 in every test and tracking errors up to two orders of magnitude lower than the baselines. The agent logs show that these agents autonomously extract dynamic performance indices, such as settling time and damping, and relate them to specific control parameters, decomposing the tuning problem into physically interpretable sub-problems. The benchmark is publicly available at this https URL.

papers.title: LeanSparse: Memory-Efficient Serving for Native Sparse-Attention LLMs
papers.abstract: Sparse attention limits the history read by each query, but serving long contexts still requires substantial GPU memory. Existing KV offloading systems retain the full history of indexer keys on GPU, limiting decode concurrency. Prefill's temporary memory demand can further delay admission even when enough memory remains for the same request's subsequent decode. We present LeanSparse, a serving system that reduces both decode's persistent memory use and prefill's temporary memory demand. Our design exploits two observations: prefill consumes historical data one layer at a time, and decode can identify promising candidates before comparing their original indexer scores. During prefill, LeanSparse streams layer histories through two reusable GPU buffers, overlapping next-layer loading with ongoing model computation. During decode, coarse-to-fine indexing searches compact representations and retrieves original indexer keys only for candidate refinement. Separate indexer key and KV caches reuse data across generation steps. We implement LeanSparse in SGLang and evaluate it on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. At 950K context length, LeanSparse supports 2.95$\times$ as many concurrent requests and achieves 2.14$\times$ decode throughput over HiSparse. On multi-turn Open-SWE traces, it reduces median time to first token from 21.6 to 0.6s and median session completion time by 17.7% relative to ECHO.

papers.title: Right Tool, Wrong Parameters: Defending LLM Agents Against Parameter Poisoning
papers.abstract: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) poses a critical threat to LLM agents. Existing defenses largely focus on whether an injection induces a new tool invocation or unintended action. In this paper, we study a different attack surface, parameter poisoning, where the attacker preserves the intended action but manipulates one or more tool arguments, such as a recipient or other task-critical value. Such attacks are difficult to detect because no new action is introduced, while parameter changes themselves are often legitimate parts of the user's request. Our key insight is that the legitimacy of a parameter change should be determined by the trust of the information flow that produces it under the user query. The query induces a task-specific trust hierarchy over available information fields: some are trusted to determine particular parameters, while others should have little or no influence. Based on this insight, we propose AuthorityFlow, a three-stage parameter-level defense. First, it interprets the user query to construct a task-specific trust hierarchy over the information fields available to the agent. Second, for each tool argument, it traces the information flow that produces its current value and attributes the value to its supporting field. Finally, it accepts the value only when that field is trusted to determine the parameter under the current task, allowing high-trust changes while flagging low-trust influence as potential parameter poisoning. We further introduce FactAuthBench for evaluating parameter poisoning in LLM agents. Without defense, the attack success rate reaches 93.06%. AuthorityFlow reduces it to 9.03%, while retaining 82.64% benign task utility compared with 90.28% without defense. Our results show that effective IPI defense requires reasoning not only about what action an agent takes, but also about which information is trusted to determine its parameters.

translation.abstract: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) poses a critical threat to LLM agents. Existing defenses largely focus on whether an injection induces a new tool invocation or unintended action. In this paper, we study a different attack surface, parameter poisoning, where the attacker preserves the intended action but manipulates one or more tool arguments, such as a recipient or other task-critical value. Such attacks are difficult to detect because no new action is introduced, while parameter changes themselves are often legitimate parts of the user's request. Our key insight is that the legitimacy of a parameter change should be determined by the trust of the information flow that produces it under the user query. The query induces a task-specific trust hierarchy over available information fields: some are trusted to determine particular parameters, while others should have little or no influence. Based on this insight, we propose AuthorityFlow, a three-stage parameter-level defense. First, it interprets the user query to construct a task-specific trust hierarchy over the information fields available to the agent. Second, for each tool argument, it traces the information flow that produces its current value and attributes the value to its supporting field. Finally, it accepts the value only when that field is trusted to determine the parameter under the current task, allowing high-trust changes while flagging low-trust influence as potential parameter poisoning. We further introduce FactAuthBench for evaluating parameter poisoning in LLM agents. Without defense, the attack success rate reaches 93.06%. AuthorityFlow reduces it to 9.03%, while retaining 82.64% benign task utility compared with 90.28% without defense. Our results show that effective IPI defense requires reasoning not only about what action an agent takes, but also about which information is trusted to determine its parameters.

papers.title: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries
papers.abstract: MIMIC is one of the most widely used public hospital datasets for machine learning on electronic health records, yet clinically important information, such as past medical history, allergies, and diagnostic findings, remains confined to free-text discharge summaries. Studies requiring this information must therefore build their own extraction pipelines, duplicating substantial effort across projects. We release MIMIC-Note-Extract (MNE), a large-scale dataset that uses a hybrid extraction pipeline combining deterministic parsing with schema-guided large language model generation to transform 16 sections from 300,720 discharge summaries into structured tables. MNE adds information that has no structured MIMIC counterpart and enriches related tables with broader coverage and greater clinical detail, including 10 times more patient-history entries and medication histories for more than twice as many admissions. Validation by medical doctors confirms extraction accuracy above 92% across sections. Using MNE, we construct a clinical decision-making benchmark for LLM agents, demonstrating how reusable structured representations of clinical narratives reduce data curation effort.

papers.title: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records
papers.abstract: Identifying the primary diagnosis alone does not fully characterize a model's diagnosis-generation performance. We introduce CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark for prioritized diagnosis generation from real-world Chinese cardiovascular inpatient records. It contains 3,262 de-identified cases, with 2,174 for training and 1,088 for evaluation, linking clinical narratives and textual ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses standardized to ICD-10. An English translation of the evaluation set supports aligned cross-lingual comparison. Our evaluation protocol combines terminology normalization and rank-aware scoring to separately assess primary-diagnosis identification, reference-diagnosis coverage, and list precision. Evaluation across 36 systems shows that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily imply higher list precision against discharge references. We also provide CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline combining entity normalization, constrained graph retrieval, and guideline evidence. In a staged comparison of three baseline models, supervised fine-tuning plus the agent achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone, representing a system-level gain. These results measure retrospective agreement with recorded diagnoses; agreement between metric rankings and physician judgments remains to be validated. CardioVascBench supports research on diagnosis prioritization and knowledge-enhanced generation.

translation.title: CardioVascBench：基于真实世界中文心血管病历的优先级诊断生成
translation.abstract: 仅识别首要诊断并不能完全刻画模型的诊断生成性能。我们提出CardioVascBench，一个从真实世界中文心血管住院病历进行优先级诊断生成的回顾性基准。它包含3,262个去标识化病例，其中2,174个用于训练、1,088个用于评估，将临床叙述和文本心电图（ECG）报告与经专家验证、按ICD-10标准化的有序出院诊断相关联。评估集的英文翻译版本支持对齐的跨语言比较。我们的评估协议结合术语归一化与排序感知打分，分别评估首要诊断识别、参考诊断覆盖率和列表精确率。对36个系统的评估表明，首要诊断准确率更高并不一定意味着相对出院参考的列表精确率更高。我们还提供了CardioKG-Agent，一个结合实体归一化、受限图检索和指南证据的知识增强基线。在三个基线模型的分阶段比较中，监督微调加该Agent比单纯微调的平均综合得分高73.5%，代表了一种系统级提升。这些结果衡量的是与已记录诊断的回顾性一致性；指标排名与医生判断之间的一致性仍有待验证。CardioVascBench支持诊断优先级排序和知识增强生成方面的研究。
translation.brief: 解决仅用首要诊断无法评估诊断生成模型排序能力的问题，构建中文心血管病历优先级诊断生成基准，并通过术语归一化与排序感知打分协议及知识增强基线进行评估。

papers.title: When Ground Truth Is Not Ground Truth: Automatic Labeling for Hallucination Detection
papers.abstract: Hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) remain a major challenge, as they can produce misleading, factually incorrect, or unverifiable information, thereby undermining their trustworthiness and reliability. However, reliable ground-truth labels remain a key challenge in evaluating hallucination detectors. Recent studies often construct labels automatically by comparing model generations with reference answers using similarity metrics such as BLEURT. This implicitly treats BLEURT similarity as a proxy for hallucination, despite its English-centric supervision, unbounded score range, and design as a similarity metric rather than a factuality measure, making threshold-based ground-truth construction potentially unreliable. Through comprehensive experiments using 15 automatic supervision judges, seven hallucination detection baselines, two generator models, two QA datasets, and five languages, we demonstrate that detector performance varies substantially with the choice of supervision judge. Human validation reveals substantial differences in labeling reliability, with QGen-9B achieving the lowest overall misclassification rate (12.86%), while BLEURT and BLEURT-n exhibit rates of 47.23% and 47.32%, respectively. Our findings highlight the limitations of automatic similarity-based labeling and the need for more reliable judging methods that better capture semantic and factual correctness.

translation.title: 当真值并非真值：面向幻觉检测的自动标注
translation.abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）中的幻觉仍是一个重大挑战，因为它们可能产生误导性、事实错误或无法验证的信息，从而损害其可信度和可靠性。然而，可靠的真值标注仍是评估幻觉检测器的关键难题。近期研究通常通过使用BLEURT等相似度指标将模型生成与参考答案进行比较来自动构建标签。这隐含地将BLEURT相似度视为幻觉的代理，尽管其监督以英语为中心、分数范围无界，且设计初衷是相似度指标而非事实性度量，使得基于阈值的真值构建可能不可靠。通过使用15个自动监督裁判、7个幻觉检测基线、2个生成器模型、2个QA数据集和5种语言的综合实验，我们证明检测器性能随监督裁判的选择而有很大差异。人工验证揭示了标注可靠性存在显著差异，其中QGen-9B实现了最低的总体误分类率（12.86%），而BLEURT和BLEURT-n的误分类率分别高达47.23%和47.32%。我们的发现凸显了基于相似度的自动标注的局限性，以及需要能更好捕捉语义和事实正确性的更可靠裁判方法。
translation.brief: 解决幻觉检测中基于BLEURT等相似度指标的自动标注不可靠的问题，通过大规模多裁判、多语言实验和人工验证揭示相似度标注的误分类率并主张使用更可靠的裁判方法。

papers.title: Proving the Wrong Program: Miscompilations as a Threat to zkVM Guarantees
papers.abstract: A zero-knowledge virtual machine (zkVM) lets an untrusted prover convince a verifier that a program, typically Rust compiled to RISC-V, ran correctly. The proof covers the compiled binary, so a miscompilation can make a correct zkVM produce a valid proof of a computation that differs from the developer's source. We present the first empirical study of miscompilation as a threat to zkVM guarantees, on the production zkVMs SP1 and Jolt. We assemble 88 known rustc and LLVM miscompilations with Rust reproducers, using an LLM agent to recover Rust triggers for 60 of 124 LLVM bugs reported only as LLVM IR. Many of the bugs carry over to zkVMs: 48 of the 88 make a guest commit a wrong output on SP1 and 46 on Jolt, including the same 15 rustc bugs on both. Most bugs that do not reproduce never reach the faulty code on the zkVM's target, e.g. because they need an instruction-set extension. Existing guest programs are rarely affected by accident. Across 13 guests of 10 popular SP1 projects, the buggy and the fixed compiler produce byte-identical binaries in 447 of the 552 guest-bug pairs that build, and the other 105 have the same code or agree on every input we ran. An attacker who contributes code to a guest, however, can trigger these bugs on purpose. For about $40 per project, an LLM agent found patches that look like ordinary optimisations, preserve the behaviour of the guest's source, and expose a known bug in 12 of 366 project-bug pairs, across 11 of 20 projects. In four cases the guest commits a wrong output, including an Ethereum client that rejects a valid block, and in the other eight it fails on a valid input. Reviewing or formally verifying the zkVM or the guest's source cannot catch such a patch, because both are correct. zkVM projects should treat their compiler as part of their trusted base and track the known bugs of their toolchain.

translation.title: 证明错误的程序：误编译对zkVM保证的威胁
translation.abstract: 零知识虚拟机（zkVM）允许不受信任的证明者说服验证者某个程序——通常是从Rust编译到RISC-V——正确运行。证明针对的是编译后的二进制，因此一次误编译可能使正确的zkVM为不同于开发者源代码的计算产生有效证明。我们首次对误编译作为zkVM保证的威胁进行了实证研究，对象是生产级zkVM SP1和Jolt。我们收集了88个带有Rust复现用例的已知rustc和LLVM误编译缺陷，并使用LLM Agent为124个仅以LLVM IR形式报告的LLVM bug中的60个恢复了Rust触发器。许多bug会波及zkVM：88个中有48个使guest在SP1上提交错误输出，46个在Jolt上如此，其中包括在两者上都复现的相同的15个rustc bug。大多数未复现的bug在zkVM的目标上从未到达缺陷代码，例如因为它们需要指令集扩展。现有guest程序很少偶然受影响。然而，向guest贡献代码的攻击者可以故意触发这些bug。每个项目约花费40美元，LLM Agent在366个项目-bug对中的12对（涉及20个项目中的11个）中找到了看似普通优化、保持guest源代码行为但暴露已知bug的补丁。其中有4例guest提交了错误输出，包括一个拒绝有效区块的以太坊客户端，另外8例则在有效输入上失败。审查或形式化验证zkVM或guest源代码都无法发现此类补丁，因为二者都是正确的。zkVM项目应将其编译器视为可信计算基的一部分，并跟踪其工具链的已知bug。
translation.brief: 首次实证研究误编译如何威胁zkVM的安全性证明，通过收集已知rustc/LLVM缺陷并用LLM Agent构造看似正常的恶意补丁，证明攻击者可诱使zkVM为偏离源码的计算产生有效证明。

papers.title: SPOD: Recovering Suppressed Temporal Evidence in Video-LLMs via Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition
papers.abstract: Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have achieved strong performance on many video understanding tasks, yet remain vulnerable to temporal hallucination in time-sensitive reasoning scenarios such as scene transition understanding and event ordering. Existing solutions either require costly retraining or introduce inefficient multi-pass inference and external supervision at test time. In this work, we show that temporal evidence is already encoded in Video-LLM hidden representations but is not fully exploited during standard inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition (SPOD), a training-free framework that recovers suppressed temporal evidence through analytical hidden-state manipulation in a single forward pass. SPOD consists of two components: Frame Distinctiveness Analysis (FDA), which identifies salient frames from middle-layer hidden-state geometry, and Temporal Delta Subspace (TDS), which constructs orthogonal temporal and prior subspaces from weighted inter-frame hidden-state differences. By decomposing final hidden states into temporal, prior, and residual components and rescaling them independently, SPOD enhances dynamic information, suppresses static appearance bias, and preserves complementary information. Experiments on VidHalluc, EventHallusion, and VideoMMMU show that SPOD consistently outperforms strong inference-time baselines across temporal reasoning tasks and model architectures while retaining near-vanilla inference efficiency. These results suggest that improving temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs may depend not only on additional supervision, but also on recovering temporal evidence already present in their internal representations. Our code is available at this https URL.

translation.title: SPOD：通过单次前向正交分解恢复Video-LLM中被抑制的时间证据
translation.abstract: 视频大语言模型（Video-LLM）在许多视频理解任务上已取得强劲表现，但在场景转换理解和事件排序等时间敏感推理场景中仍易受时间幻觉影响。现有方案要么需要代价高昂的重新训练，要么在测试时引入低效的多轮推理和外部监督。在这项工作中，我们证明时间证据已经编码在Video-LLM的隐藏表示中，但在标准推理过程中未被充分利用。基于这一观察，我们提出单次前向正交分解（SPOD），一个免训练框架，通过在单次前向传播中对隐藏状态进行解析式操作来恢复被抑制的时间证据。SPOD包含两个组件：帧独特性分析（FDA），从中层隐藏状态几何中识别显著帧；时间差分子空间（TDS），从加权的帧间隐藏状态差异中构建正交的时间子空间和先验子空间。通过将最终隐藏状态分解为时间、先验和残差分量并独立重缩放，SPOD增强了动态信息、抑制了静态外观偏差，并保留了互补信息。在VidHalluc、EventHallusion和VideoMMMU上的实验表明，SPOD在时间推理任务和模型架构上持续优于强推理时基线，同时保持接近原始的推理效率。这些结果表明，改进Video-LLM的时间推理可能不仅依赖额外监督，还依赖恢复其内部表示中已存在的时间证据。代码可通过此https链接获取。
translation.brief: 解决Video-LLM在时间敏感推理中的时间幻觉问题，提出免训练的SPOD框架，通过单次前向传播对隐藏状态进行正交分解与重缩放来恢复被抑制的时间证据。

papers.title: Logarithmic Comparison-Query Complexity for EF1 Allocations
papers.abstract: We study the comparison-query complexity of computing allocations that are envy-free up to one item (EF1) for $n$ agents with heterogeneous additive preferences over $m$ indivisible items. In this model, the algorithm may only query which of two bundles an agent prefers, without ever observing numerical valuations or costs. Prior work established $O(\log m)$ query bounds for at most three agents, leaving open whether query complexity logarithmic in $m$ is achievable for every fixed $n \ge 4$. We resolve this open question in the affirmative: for every fixed $n\ge2$, we design algorithms that compute EF1 allocations using $O(\log m)$ comparison queries, matching the known $\Omega(\log m)$ lower bound. Our results hold for both chores with nonnegative costs and goods with nonnegative valuations.

translation.title: EF1分配的对数比较查询复杂度
translation.abstract: 我们研究在$n$个代理对$m$个不可分割物品具有异构可加偏好的情况下，计算免除嫉妒至多一个物品（EF1）分配的比较查询复杂度。在该模型中，算法只能查询某个代理更偏好两个捆绑包中的哪一个，而无法观测到数值化的估值或成本。先前的工作为至多三个代理确立了$O(\log m)$的查询界，对于每个固定的$n \ge 4$是否能实现关于$m$的对数查询复杂度仍悬而未决。我们对这一开放问题给出了肯定回答：对于每个固定的$n\ge2$，我们设计了使用$O(\log m)$次比较查询计算EF1分配的算法，与已知的$\Omega(\log m)$下界相匹配。我们的结果对具有非负成本的 chores 和具有非负估值的 goods 均成立。
translation.brief: 解决任意固定代理数$n\ge2$下EF1分配在仅允许比较查询模型中的查询复杂度问题，设计出$O(\log m)$次查询的算法并匹配下界。

papers.title: When Should an LLM Steering Edit Depend on the Input?
papers.abstract: An activation steering edit should depend on the input exactly when the destination varies \emph{inside} the class a query requests, and that is measurable before any rule is fitted or applied. Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) adds one fixed direction to every input, the difference of the class means. Conditioning it on the requested class accounts for the between-class variation in the required displacement and leaves the within-class variation untouched, which no rule that reads only the source state can express. We study the impact of increasing input-dependence in the steering edit, moving from a difference of means to a destination retrieved per query --- the mean of the $k$ stored states nearest the query, inside the requested class --- in which the two baselines are endpoints: at $k$ equal to the class size the retrieved rule \emph{is} the class-conditional difference of means. We measure input-dependent steering on six substitution corpora that vary in whether the edit changes a word or a clause, and on an external benchmark, and find that input-dependent steering outperforms fixed-direction steering when the destination varies within the class. Retrieval wins at every layer of every substitution corpus in two models, and the level of input-dependence needed governs how to apply it: word-level edits are best made in the first tenth of the network from a few neighbours, clause-level edits at any depth from the class mean. Where the class already determines the answer the class mean suffices and retrieval only matches it, though a fixed direction still fails there. Four quantities computed from the states alone identify the regime in which the edit should be applied.

papers.title: TriMedium: A Cross-Medium Simulator for Embodied Networking Across Air-Ground-Sea
papers.abstract: Embodied intelligent applications have expanded from air and ground into maritime environments, where missions such as coastal reporting require coordination among underwater sensing, surface gateways, and aerial relays. Yet field trials remain costly, and existing simulation tools make it difficult to study how cross-medium communication affects cooperation among these platforms. We present TriMedium, an integrated Air-Ground-Sea simulator for cross-medium embodied networking. TriMedium has three design elements. First, it provides a shared three-dimensional world where aerial, terrestrial, and underwater entities coexist, so underwater agent motion and visual observations stay geometrically consistent with air and ground nodes. Second, it uses a common simulation clock that preserves observation timestamps while scheduling delayed communication and computation, clarifying when the shore receiver obtains each observation. Third, modular quantization and compression interfaces accommodate heterogeneous telemetry and image pipelines, while integrity checks separate intentional lossy distortion from incomplete or corrupted delivery. Three case studies validate TriMedium. Multimodal data delivery tests telemetry and image pipelines, scene construction examines cross-domain spatial consistency, and positioning assesses geometric accuracy under delayed communication. Together, they show TriMedium enables embodied networking by quantifying cross-medium delivery dynamics and fidelity across heterogeneous payloads.

papers.title: TactiNavi: Serving and Revising an LLM Game Coach with Explicit Strategy Conditions
papers.abstract: A deployed LLM coaching agent answers requests whose correct response depends on player state and game version, so advice that is right for one player can be wrong for the next. We describe TactiNavi, the serving system behind the LLM coach of a commercial open-world game, which makes strategy applicability an explicit artifact shared by offline compilation, online execution, failure diagnosis, and release. An offline compiler turns versioned game evidence and expert guidance into strategy packages with explicit prerequisites, the serving plane evaluates those prerequisites as three-valued conditions over structured player state and records decision traces, and a control plane uses the resulting condition-rule dependencies to validate revisions on held-out traffic before release. In a retrospective evaluation of 1,122 logged coaching turns from three deployment periods, condition-bearing packages raise correctness from 57.9% to 82.0% over atomic facts and reduce strategy misapplication under changed player state from 18.1% to 10.4%, while trace-based claim verification reaches 86.4% precision at a median reply latency of 2.07 s. The deployment also showed that most apparent fixes are generation noise, because an unchanged-system rerun recovers 38.4% of failing turns and only one of 15 shipped revision units passes the release checks retrospectively. We distill these results into lessons on treating applicability as a first-class serving object, sizing traces for later diagnosis, and building the null model into the release path.

papers.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Submodular Trajectory Rewards
papers.abstract: We study cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled dynamics and a monotone submodular reward function over joint trajectories. Due to the non-additive reward, an optimal policy may depend on the history of all agents. This dependence makes exact optimization exponential in the horizon and the number of agents. To overcome this challenge while retaining theoretical guarantees, we introduce pre-window curvature $c_m$, which quantifies how states visited more than $m$ steps earlier reduce current marginal gains. Using this curvature to control the error from restricting the policy of each agent to depend only on its last $m+1$ states, we propose a greedy algorithm that exploits the decoupled dynamics to optimize local policies sequentially. For fixed $m$, the algorithm achieves a $\frac{1-c_m}{2-c_m}$ approximation guarantee up to estimation error, and its computation time is polynomial in the number of agents and the horizon. We recover the known $1/2$-factor approximation for time-additive rewards and obtain an approximation factor no smaller than the known total-curvature bound for a single agent. We formulate multi-agent traffic monitoring as an example of this framework and evaluate our algorithm on it.

translation.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Submodular Trajectory Rewards
translation.abstract: We study cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled dynamics and a monotone submodular reward function over joint trajectories. Due to the non-additive reward, an optimal policy may depend on the history of all agents. This dependence makes exact optimization exponential in the horizon and the number of agents. To overcome this challenge while retaining theoretical guarantees, we introduce pre-window curvature $c_m$, which quantifies how states visited more than $m$ steps earlier reduce current marginal gains. Using this curvature to control the error from restricting the policy of each agent to depend only on its last $m+1$ states, we propose a greedy algorithm that exploits the decoupled dynamics to optimize local policies sequentially. For fixed $m$, the algorithm achieves a $\frac{1-c_m}{2-c_m}$ approximation guarantee up to estimation error, and its computation time is polynomial in the number of agents and the horizon. We recover the known $1/2$-factor approximation for time-additive rewards and obtain an approximation factor no smaller than the known total-curvature bound for a single agent. We formulate multi-agent traffic monitoring as an example of this framework and evaluate our algorithm on it.

papers.title: Learning to Rank Explanations for Recommendation with Language Models
papers.abstract: Recommender systems are ubiquitous on the Web, making understandable explanations essential for users. Although large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate natural-language justifications, evaluating their factual grounding and personalized relevance remains challenging. Statement-level ranking offers an alternative by selecting concise, review-derived explanations, enabling fine-grained and reproducible evaluation using established ranking metrics. However, existing statement ranking methods largely rely on collaborative representations, while semantic enhancements often fail to outperform simple user-history popularity baselines. Moreover, directly adapting language models for personalized statement ranking remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce LMStaR (Language Models for Statement Ranking), a fully text-based framework that formulates personalized explanation ranking as dense retrieval. A query encoder represents the user's interaction history and target-item metadata, while a statement encoder maps candidate explanations into a shared embedding space. Both encoders are jointly adapted through multi-positive contrastive learning to learn personalized relevance. Experiments on Amazon Beauty, Amazon Toys, and Yelp show that LMStaR achieves the highest NDCG@1 across all three domains, outperforming CLER by 1.06--8.25 points (+11.8--65.9%). It also leads top-five ranking on both Amazon datasets, although CLER remains stronger on Yelp. Task-specific adaptation improves all five evaluated backbones and transfers across domains without target-domain fine-tuning. Counterfactual analyses further reveal the importance of user-specific histories. These findings highlight the potential of task-adapted language models for personalized explanation ranking.
